question.text: The FATF's "Black List" refers to countries or jurisdictions with:

answer.text: Serious strategic deficiencies to counter money laundering, terrorist financing, and financing of proliferation
The strongest AML/CFT frameworks in the world
Countries that have voluntarily exited the FATF membership
Countries with the highest GDP but no AML laws

explanation.text: The Logic: The FATF Black List identifies countries or jurisdictions with serious strategic deficiencies to counter ML/TF/PF. FATF calls on members to apply enhanced due diligence and, in the most serious cases, counter-measures to protect the international financial system from the ongoing ML/TF/PF risks emanating from such jurisdictions. The Trap: The Black List identifies the WEAKEST jurisdictions, not the strongest. It is not a voluntary exit list or a GDP-based categorisation. Note: For clients with exposure to a black-listed jurisdiction, country-risk assessment and enhanced measures for high-risk jurisdictions apply, as reflected in the checked workbook pages on country/geographic risk.
